security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD's intc driver (sys/riscv/riscv/intc.c) registers all 16 interrupt sources (0-15) uniformly with INTR_ISRCF_PPI, but interrupt 14 is now defined by the AIA spec as a local interrupt (LAMBI/asynchronous memory buffer) with distinct priority and delegation semantics from standard major interrupts. The kernel has no IRQ_* enumeration constant for interrupt 14 (sys/riscv/include/intr.h:44-55 only defines 0-11), no LAMBI-specific handling in the trap dispatcher, and no awareness of interrupt 14 in the bhyve VMM (sys/riscv/vmm/riscv.h:56-68) for virtual interrupt filtering. If M-mode firmware delegates a LAMBI interrupt to S-mode, the kernel will dispatch it as a generic PPI through a blind scause-based lookup (intc.c:276-281) without any Ssamb-specific state management, potentially misinterpreting or losing asynchronous memory buffer events that hardware expects the kernel to acknowledge.
security_spec.summary: Interrupt 14 repurposed from reserved to 'asynchronous memory buffer interrupt' (LAMBI) as a local interrupt per AIA; FreeBSD has no enumeration constant, no Ssamb-aware dispatch, and no VMM virtualization for this interrupt, risking unhandled local interrupt storms or silent loss of memory buffer events
